header.text: The letter i is a vowel. When i is followed by just consonants, i does not say its name. It makes a short i sound (/ĭ/) instead.
When i is followed by a consonant and a silent e, i says its name. It makes a long i sound (/ī/).
When i is followed by another vowel, the two vowels can make a vowel team. In vowel teams that start with i, i says its name. It makes a long i sound. The other vowel is silent.

textContent.text: Jean owns a gray rowboat. She will take the boat up the creek. Her friend Moe will go too. Jean and Moe can not wait.
They race to the boat. A breeze blows, and the boat starts to float.
The boat floats past a log. "Look Moe!" screams Jean. "I see three toads on that log."
The toads let out low, slow croaks. The girls leap up to see the toads croak.
Uh-oh! The boat sways and tips over. "Now we are soaked!" says Moe.
Jean smiles and says, "It's okay. We will dry off as we row the boat back home."
